hero.subtitle_html: Ridge walk via Iltios cable car — SAC T3 · ~1000 m gain · ~12 km · ~5–6 h

intro_html:
"Chäserrugg is the highest of the seven flat-topped Churfirsten peaks, their distinctive table-top silhouette visible from across north-eastern Switzerland. The ridge walk above the treeline offers one of the most spectacular panoramas in the Swiss Alps: Walensee shimmering blue in the valley, Bodensee glittering on the northern horizon, and the Appenzell and Vorarlberg Alps rolling east."
— Route notes

The Churfirsten (7 peaks east to west: Chäserrugg, Hinterrugg, Zuestoll, Brisi, Selun, Frümsel, Gauschla) form a near-horizontal limestone wall above Walensee. Chäserrugg (2262 m) is the easternmost and highest, linked to neighbouring Hinterrugg (2306 m) by a narrow ridge. The standard route uses the Unterwasser–Iltios cable car (1317 m) to bypass 400 m of forest, then follows the open Churfirsten crest with moderate exposure to the summit. A Herzog & de Meuron–designed Bergrestaurant sits at the top — coffee with a sheer-drop view included.

routes_subtitle: (from the SAC Route Portal and local guides)

routes.title_html: 1. Via Iltios cable car → Selun → Chäserrugg — standard route
bullets_html: Start: Unterwasser, Toggenburg (~910 m). Take the cable car to Iltios (1317 m) to save ~400 m of forest ascent.
From Iltios, follow the broad ridge path north-east, gaining altitude steadily on open alpine terrain above the treeline.
Pass via Selun (~2205 m), one of the Churfirsten ridge peaks, with views opening toward Walensee.
Final push to Chäserrugg summit (2262 m): some exposed ledges and rocky sections (T3).
Return the same way, or continue to Hinterrugg (2306 m) for a ridge extension.
Total from Iltios: ~12 km round-trip, ~700 m gain, ~4–5 h. From Unterwasser: ~1000 m gain, ~5–6 h.
From Chäserrugg, the narrow ridge to Hinterrugg (2306 m) is the highest point of the Churfirsten.
Exposed traverse with good holds — stay on the marked path. Adds ~1–2 h and requires sure-footedness.
Descent back via Iltios cable car — confirm last departure time before committing.
The classic multi-peak traverse covers all seven Churfirsten summits to the Gauschla (2075 m) in the west.
Very long day (10+ h); T4 experience and route-finding ability required on unmarked sections.
Descent to Flums or Unterterzen (Walensee) on the north side, or return transport from Walenstadt.
Not recommended as a first Churfirsten outing — do the T3 standard route first.

getting_there.by_car_html: Drive to Unterwasser (Toggenburg, SG). Parking at or near the cable car base station. The valley road runs from Wattwil (A1 junction) or from Bad Ragaz via Flums and the Walensee north shore.
getting_there.by_pt_html:
• Train: Zürich HB → Wattwil (~55 min, S-Bahn S7 or IR 15 toward Chur).
  • Postbus 740: Wattwil → Unterwasser (~35 min, several per hour in summer).
  • Total door-to-door from Zürich: ~2 h. Buy cable car ticket on site at Unterwasser.
  • Plan via sbb.ch.

day_plans.title: Day Plan — standard T3 via Iltios cable car
rows: Arrive Unterwasser cable car station (~910 m)
Cable car up to Iltios (1317 m)
Start hiking from Iltios toward Selun on the ridge path
Selun (~2205 m) — views open over Walensee
Summit Chäserrugg (2262 m) — ~3 h from Iltios
Lunch / coffee at Bergrestaurant Chäserrugg (reserve ahead in high season)
Cable car down to Unterwasser (check last departure!)
day_plans.footer_html: Start earlier (06:15 train) if combining with Hinterrugg or if afternoon thunderstorms are forecast. The Churfirsten crest is fully exposed — descent is mandatory if storms develop.

lapse_rate.example_html: Example: valley forecast 12–22 °C → summit ≈ 3 °C to 13 °C. Wind chill on the exposed limestone ridge adds further cooling.

sources_html: MeteoSwiss — most accurate Swiss forecast (use Unterwasser or Wildhaus point).
Meteoblue Unterwasser — hourly forecast + nearby webcam links.
Thunderstorms in forecast → do not go. The Churfirsten limestone ridge gives zero shelter and storms form quickly in Toggenburg.
weather.season_html: Summer hike only. Best window: late June to mid-October, depending on snow. Ridge snow can persist into early June; autumn can bring early snow from September. Check SLF in shoulder season.

webcams.label: Wildhaus / Gamserrugg — looking north toward Churfirsten from ~1090 m; best real-time visibility indicator for the Toggenburg area.
Meteoblue webcams near Unterwasser (link only — Meteoblue blocks iframe embedding).

takeaways_html: The cable car from Unterwasser to Iltios is strongly recommended — it saves 400 m of steep forest and opens 4+ hours of ridge hiking. Verify opening dates on churfirsten.ch before going.

The ridge path from Iltios to Chäserrugg is well-marked but includes several exposed ledge sections with a significant drop to the north (Walensee, ~1800 m below). Vertigo-prone hikers should assess the T3 rating carefully.

Summit panorama is exceptional on clear days: Walensee and Walenstadt directly below to the north, Bodensee on the northern horizon, Säntis and Appenzell Alps to the east, Graubünden Alps (Ringelspitz, Piz Sardona) to the south-east.

The Bergrestaurant Chäserrugg (Herzog & de Meuron design, 2016) is a unique architectural highlight — excellent coffee and a terrace with sheer-drop views over Walensee. Reserve a table for lunch in high season.
Cattle graze on the Iltios alp in mid-summer — give mother cows with calves wide berth.

reports.title: Chäserrugg via Iltios — Churfirsten Klassiker
bullets_html: Cable car to Iltios, then open ridge path with expanding views south toward the Glarus Alps.
Selun passed as an intermediate high point before the final exposed approach to Chäserrugg.
Lunch at the Bergrestaurant, leisurely descent — a perfect half-day alpine hike from Zürich.

reports.title: Chäserrugg + Hinterrugg — Doppelgipfel im Churfirsten
bullets_html: Continue from Chäserrugg along the narrow ridge to Hinterrugg (2306 m) — the highest Churfirsten peak.
Exposed crest with good holds and red-white waymarks; more committing than the approach.
Adds about 1.5 h; descent back to Iltios before last cable car — watch the time.

reports.title: Churfirsten-Traverse: alle 7 Gipfel
bullets_html: Full traverse of all seven Churfirsten peaks: Chäserrugg, Hinterrugg, Zuestoll, Brisi, Selun, Frümsel, Gauschla.
Very long day (10+ h); T4 experience and route-finding required on unmarked ridge sections.
Two-car logistics or bus/train return from Flums or Unterterzen on the Walensee north shore.

gear.title: Mandatory
items_html: Sturdy hiking boots (B-grade, ankle support) — limestone ridge slippery when wet
2–3 L water (no reliable sources on the upper ridge)
Sun: hat, sunglasses, SPF 30+ (exposed ridge, high UV)
Layers: base + insulating + windproof / rainproof shell (ridge wind)
Hat + gloves (summit often 5–10 °C cooler than valley with wind chill)
Phone with offline SwissTopo map + GPX
Cash / card for cable car and Bergrestaurant

gear.title: Recommended
items_html: Trekking poles (helpful on the steep descent from Selun)

gear.title: Hinterrugg / full traverse only
items_html: Helmet (for full traverse on unmarked ridge sections)
Significantly more time and an early start

safety_html: Exposure: the Chäserrugg ridge has a steep northern drop (~1800 m to Walensee); several ledge sections on the T3 route. A slip can be very serious.
Limestone: excellent grip when dry — extremely slippery when wet. Do not attempt in or just after rain.
Thunderstorms: the Churfirsten crest offers zero shelter. Descend immediately if storms develop — they form quickly in Toggenburg, often by early afternoon.
Cable car last departure: missing it means a long, steep forest descent. Check the schedule at the valley station and build in buffer time.
Cattle: mother cows with calves graze on the Iltios alp in summer — give them space.
Phone reception: generally good on the summit; can be patchy on descent paths. Download SwissTopo maps offline.
This is a summer / autumn route. Winter and spring involve avalanche terrain and snow-covered limestone — very different gear and experience required.

disclaimer_html: Compiled from the SAC Route Portal, German Wikipedia, hikr.org, and knowledge of the Toggenburg / Churfirsten area. Not professional mountain-safety advice. Conditions in the Alps change rapidly. Always re-check MeteoSwiss, SAC situation warnings, and cable car operating status before setting out. The Churfirsten limestone ridge is unforgiving in wet weather — if in doubt, postpone.
